summary: Frontend-only test of the six realm surfaces (/app /os /floor /studio /portal /vault) + /hub strip + /revsys admin key. CRITICAL BLOCKER FOUND: the realm-client.js shim's auth.getSession() reads `me.user` but the backend /api/auth/me returns the user fields at the TOP LEVEL (no `.user` wrapper). Consequence: even with a valid mfa_verified session cookie, every surface calls ensureAuth() → getSession() returns { data:{ session:null } } → surface renders the in-page 'Director sign-in / Send magic link' gate instead of the real shell. This blocks tests for /app (add lead, run cycle, approvals), /os (nav + widget), /floor (team_view / log call), /studio (no-air gate), /portal (director view), and any authed features of /vault. Verified /api/realm/summary and /api/auth/me directly with the seeded session (both return 200 with the correct shape and mfa_verified=true), and verified /hub strip renders 0s from /api/realm/summary and adminKey inputs on /hub + /revsys start EMPTY (no yabbai-director-key prefill).

Do NOT redirect to /login when unauthenticated (spec asked for /login redirect). They show an in-page 'Send magic link' gate. This magic link flow is also non-functional in this deployment (auth is Google + TOTP, not magic link). Consider swapping ensureAuth() to redirect via `location.href='/login/index.html?next='+pathname` when getSession() returns null, matching the auth model already used by /hub/settings.

rca of the issue: PRIMARY BUG: realm-client.js is a Supabase-shim written to Supabase's session shape ({data:{session:{user:{...}}}}). It fetches the network's /api/auth/me and does `if (!me || !me.user)` — but the FastAPI endpoint returns the user directly (user_id, email, mfa_verified at top level). Every call to getSession() therefore returns { session: null }, and every surface's ensureAuth() falls through to the 'Send magic link' gate even for a valid mfa_verified Director session. Reproduction: (1) seed a director+session and set the session_token cookie; (2) hit /app/index.html — you see the sign-in gate, not the pipeline shell; (3) console log `await (await fetch('/api/auth/me',{credentials:'include'})).json()` shows user_id/email present, mfa_verified:true, but no `.user` key. Mitigation: patch realm-client.js auth.getSession() to treat me itself as the user (guard on me.user_id) and return { data:{ session:{ user: me, mfa_verified: !!me.mfa_verified } } }; also short-circuit to /login when session is null instead of showing the misleading magic-link gate.
